lines.t: What if a token launch felt like a boss fight, and only real people could win it?
Community buys are broken.
Bots farm the rewards.
Snipers wait for the very last second.
And the sponsor never knows if a real community even showed up.
Not everyone can trade.
But anyone can play a game with their friends.
So we spent five days building Star Raid for Monad Metropolis.
Star Raid is a co-op raid game on a real on-chain order book.
A sponsor puts up a wall of their token.
Lil Stars holders take their seats, and break it together, live.
So who are the Lil Stars?
Lilstars, formerly Chogstar, is a digital collectible IP born on Monad.
Meet the Stars crew: Chogstar, Bunnystar, Foxstar and Bearstar.
One universe, one IP, and it's growing off-chain too, with IRL blind boxes and merch for holders.
Their motto is that everyone can be a star.
In Star Raid, your Lil Star is your seat.
Find them at lilstars.xyz, and on X at lilstarrrs.
lines.say: Find them at lil stars dot x y z, and on X at lil stars, with three R's.

lines.t: This is the lobby. The next raid, live, right here on your phone.
A sponsor sets the wall, the price cap and a USDC prize, and posts it in a few taps.
Your Lil Star is your seat. One Star, one seat. That's the whole bot defence.
Set up once, and every raid after that is one tap. No wallet popups.
When the window opens, everyone hits the wall. Every hit is a real buy.
Then the end block is drawn, every hit is checked, and if the seats hit the target, the wall breaks.
Here's how a raid plays.
A sponsor puts up a wall and a prize.
For about a minute, every seat taps HIT. Each hit buys from the wall.
The last stretch is the danger zone: the raid can end on any block in there.
Pyth draws the end block. Hits before it count. Hits after it don't.
Hit the target, the wall breaks and the seats split the prize.
Miss it, and the prize rolls into the sponsor's next raid.
Under the hood, every hit is a buy on Kuru's order book on Monad, capped at the wall price.
Cheaper asks fill first, and anything left over is cancelled and refunded in the same transaction.
The end of the raid is drawn by Pyth Entropy after the window closes, so nobody can snipe the last block.
And only seats count.
A wallet without a Lil Star can still buy, but it earns nothing.
On testnet, raid #26 broke its wall: 58 hits, 580 counted against a 500 target.
lines.say: On testnet, raid twenty-six broke its wall: fifty-eight hits, five hundred eighty counted against a five hundred target.

lines.t: We built it on Monad because a raid only feels like a game when blocks are fast.
Kuru gives us a real on-chain order book, so the wall is real liquidity, not a mock.
And Pyth Entropy gives us a fair end that nobody, not even us, can know in advance.
Right now Star Raid is live on Monad testnet.
Next, we go to mainnet.
Then passkey sign-in, so anyone can join without installing a wallet.
And more walls: any sponsor token, starting with liquid staking tokens.
We think this is something the Monad community would love to play.
This is Star Raid.
One Star.
One seat.
One wall.
Grab a seat at starraid.xyz
lines.say: Grab a seat at star raid dot x y z.
